title: Adaptive Cost Sherpa: Dynamic serving knobs for batching, cache, and quant profiles
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build an initiative-level roadmap and delivery plan (Adaptive Cost Sherpa) that provides automated, safe defaults and runtime controls for batching, prefix/KV caching, and quantization profiles. The output should be a packaged set of config recommendations + runtime autopilot behaviors that product teams can enable per-route or per-customer to reduce token cost while preserving SLOs and quality. This ticket coordinates scope, acceptance, rollout plan, and experiment matrix.
goals: Reduce average per-token serving cost by 18% for targeted PLG routes within 90 days
Provide per-route autopilot that suggests and enforces batching/caching/quant profiles with rollback safety
Ship analytics and guardrails so SRE and product can observe quality regressions and autoscale trade-offs
success_metrics: Mean per-token cost reduction (target >= 18%) measured on production cohort (routes: /generate, /chat)
Latency P95 impact <= +10% compared to baseline for enabled routes
No customer-facing regressions detected (quality alerts <= 1 per 10k requests) after canary rollout
Adoption: 30% of eligible paid customers opt into recommendations or autopilot within 60 days of GA
acceptance_criteria: Config API: route-level enable/disable with three knobs (batch_window_ms, cache_policy, quant_profile) documented
Runtime: autopilot engine evaluates traffic signals and applies recommended knob changes within SLA
Console: per-route cost/budget view and signal charts (batch size distribution, cache hit rate, quantization fallback events)
Experiment harness: A/B framework to measure cost vs quality with automated rollback triggers
Documentation: playbook for SRE and Customer Success covering rollback, incident runbook, and customer communication template
updates: 2025-02-15 - Created ticket with initial charter; linked to OKR: ECON-Reduce-Unit-Costs Q2

2025-02-27 - Decision to prioritize prefix/KV cache safety: require canary with synthetic prompt-set to detect hallucination/quality regressions
2025-03-01 - Design review: Console mocks for per-route autopilot controls; feedback: surface expected cost delta and risk score before enabling
2025-03-03 - Created experiment matrix and tagging plan; allocated Cycle 2025-W11 for pilot evaluation; synced with CS on customer pilot candidates
decision_log: 2025-02-20 - Adopt three-signal approach (batching, caching, quant) rather than chasing single-lever optimizations to maximize headroom
2025-02-25 - Use staged quant profiles (Q1: fp16->int8->int4) with runtime fallback if quality metrics cross threshold
2025-02-27 - Canary gating requires both metric-based and eval-based checks (token-level perplexity + human-reviewed prompt set) before any wide enable
2025-03-01 - Prioritize UX clarity: show estimated cost savings and expected latency delta in console before enabling autopilot per route

Run closed pilot on 3 internal routes during 2025-W11 and collect cost/quality telemetry
